articles.title: Canva lanzó Craft, su primer modelo propio de generación de imágenes con inteligencia artificial
articles.summary:
Canva presentó Craft, su primer modelo de inteligencia artificial para generar imágenes entrenado íntegramente por su propio equipo de investigación, con el que la plataforma de diseño busca competir con los sistemas de Google, OpenAI, ByteDance y Meta.
El modelo ya está disponible para todos los usuarios de Canva a nivel mundial desde la pestaña Dream Lab del menú de la aplicación, según informó la empresa en un comunicado publicado en su sala de prensa.
También puede usarse a través de la API pública de Canva, pensada para que desarrolladores integren la herramienta en plataformas de marketing, comercio electrónico o sitios de impresión.
Craft genera imágenes de hasta 2.000 píxeles de resolución en más de 30 proporciones de aspecto distintas. Canva explicó que el sistema funciona en dos etapas: primero interpreta el pedido del usuario y arma un plan de composición que define qué elementos aparecen, su escala, su jerarquía visual y el texto que debe incluirse; después, un segundo modelo traduce ese plan en la imagen final.
Esa arquitectura en dos pasos busca resolver un problema habitual de los generadores de imágenes: el texto ilegible o mal ubicado dentro de la composición. Según la empresa, separar la planificación del renderizado permite un control más preciso sobre cada elemento, de modo que se puede editar una parte de la imagen sin alterar el resto.

But Preethi Ashwath has learned to take center stage, talking about the “hearable” and wearable devices she has had a hand in developing as an analog integrated circuit designer in the consumer electronics division at Analog Devices of Wilmington, Mass.

articles.title: Microsoft’s new voice AI can start working out what you want before you finish speaking
articles.summary:
Microsoft’s new voice AI can start working out what you want before you finish speaking
“I think you said, ‘representative.’” It’s the fastest way to bypass automated speech recognition chatbots that fail to route human callers to the service they need. Achieving a human handoff to a living, breathing representative still feels like a badge of honor.
Microsoft wants to change that dynamic.
Naomi Moneypenny, senior director of product development at Microsoft Foundry Models division, blogged on October 1 to introduce three new Microsoft AI (MAI) models in Microsoft Foundry, Redmond’s app and agent model catalog and platform.
“A voice agent has to do more than hear a request and produce a reply. It has to keep the interaction moving while it listens, reasons, uses tools, and speaks. A delay at either end can turn a conversation into a series of awkward pauses,” writes Moneypenny.
Available now in Microsoft Foundry, the latest voice-centric models include MAI-Transcribe-2-Streaming, which turns live speech into text as it is spoken; MAI-Voice-2.1, an expressive multilingual text-to-speech model; and MAI-Voice-2.1-Flash, optimized for responsive, high-volume voice applications.
Partials drive incremental speech recognition

articles.title: OpenAI corta internet de suas IAs mais avançadas após falhas de segurança
articles.summary:
A OpenAI passou a treinar seus modelos de inteligência artificial (IA) mais avançados sem acesso à internet aberta após identificar falhas que permitiram a agentes de IA ultrapassar barreiras de segurança e acessar sistemas externos. A medida busca impedir que modelos em desenvolvimento explorem vulnerabilidades durante o treinamento e causem danos fora dos ambientes controlados pela empresa.
Em publicação feita nesta sexta-feira (23), a companhia explicou que reforçou os mecanismos de isolamento de seus ambientes de pesquisa e criou um sistema offline no qual os modelos podem interagir com conteúdos da web previamente indexados e armazenados em cache, sem acessar diretamente servidores externos.
A empresa havia suspendido o treinamento e a avaliação de seus modelos mais avançados em setembro, após um modelo interno explorar uma configuração incorreta e conseguir acesso limitado à internet. Depois de implementar novas proteções, a OpenAI retomou o treinamento por aprendizado por reforço e o uso interno desses modelos em 1º de outubro.
Segundo a companhia, a decisão de manter o treinamento sem acesso à internet aberta continuará em vigor até que avanços nos mecanismos de segurança justifiquem uma flexibilização.

articles.title: Bringing post-quantum cryptography to geographically fenced key management
articles.summary:
Bringing post-quantum cryptography to geographically fenced key management
Today, Cloudflare is launching a post-quantum geographically restricted key manager in support of our Data Localization Suite (DLS) in closed beta. This new PQ GeoKey Manager is a cornerstone of Cloudflare’s data sovereignty solutions, making sure that a customer's decryption keys are only accessible in their chosen geography. GeoKey Manager implements this by wrapping each decryption key such that it can only be decrypted by Cloudflare servers that are located in the allowed geography.
While general availability (GA) is planned for Q1 2027, today’s launch is an important milestone on our journey to support our customers’ data sovereignty goals while also migrating all Cloudflare products to post-quantum (PQ) cryptography.
Governments, financial institutions, healthcare providers, and defense organizations process highly sensitive data that can remain sensitive for years or decades after it is produced. Encryption is often required to protect this data. When classical, public-key encryption is used, adversaries do not immediately need a quantum computer today to put that data at risk: they can store the ciphertext and retain them until quantum computers can break the public key cryptography protecting it — an attack strategy known as harvest now, decrypt later.

articles.title: A few engineers asked IT for Linux. Then it spread to 200 machines.
articles.summary:
A few engineers asked IT for Linux. Then it spread to 200 machines.
Linux is already part of the AI developer’s desktop toolkit. Nvidia’s DGX Spark, which became available to order on October 15, 2025, runs the Ubuntu-based DGX OS. OpenAI’s Codex CLI already supports Linux, another example of AI tools meeting developers where they work.
There’s just one problem. Developers can fall in love with Linux at home. Getting enterprise IT to let them use it at work is another matter.
Angelo Huang, founder and CEO of Swif.ai, a platform that manages and secures employee devices, wants to change that. Huang tells The New Stack that giving developers Linux machines starts with giving IT teams the controls to manage and secure them.
Huang says that starting this past week, Swif began expanding its Linux device management and compliance capabilities, adding Omarchy and Linux Mint support to its roster. Swif is also optimizing the onboarding process across supported Mac, Windows, Linux, iOS, and Android environments. They claim that it now takes under 10 minutes to set up device compliance standards such as SOC 2, ISO 27001, and HIPAA.
“Linux already runs much of the infrastructure behind AI,” Huang says. “Increasingly, developers want it on their desks too. The problem isn’t that Linux can’t be secure. It’s that enterprise IT needs to be able to manage it, enforce controls, and prove those controls are working for their compliance requirements. That’s the gap we’re closing.”

articles.title: The iPhone Duo should have been an iPad
articles.summary:
We gave the iPhone Duo a 7 /10. But that wasn’t always the score we planned, and it might not be the right score forever. Such are the challenges of reviewing — and assessing — a big, new idea about the most popular smartphone in history.
The iPhone Duo should have been an iPad
On The Vergecast: Notes on an iPhone Duo review, a PHP scandal, Brendan Carr, and more.
On this episode of The Vergecast, David and Nilay debate whether the Duo deserved the score it got, and try to work through how this device might change over time. Is the outer screen, as Daring Fireball’s John Gruber suggested, the worst iPhone ever? Would it be a better product if it started as an iPad rather than an iPhone? Would we feel differently about this thing if it were simply called the iPad Duo? It’s easy to see how the Duo will improve over time, but will it ever be the phone for everyone?
After that, the hosts talk about the huge PHP cybersecurity flaw that rocked the web this week and what it means for the future of the web, AI, and everything. It was a strange week for the web in general, as the ongoing increase in AI shopping has forced retailers everywhere to figure out how they want to interact with customers — and by customers, we mean Muse agents. Then it’s time for Brendan Carr Is a Dummy, an impending reboot inside of Netflix, and some very confusing Gemini news.

articles.title: Los países están considerando prohibir las gafas inteligentes por preocupaciones de privacidad
articles.summary:
Varios países están estudiando prohibir las gafas inteligentes por el riesgo de que puedan grabar a otras personas o captar información confidencial sin que se advierta. Su uso ya está prohibido en determinados lugares, mientras que otras restricciones se consideran en diversos países.
Restricciones en espacios públicos y tribunales
Noruega se comprometió el 5 de octubre de 2026 a presentar un proyecto de ley para prohibir de forma temporal las gafas inteligentes en espacios públicos. Entre los lugares sujetos a esta consideración se incluyen los parques, las playas, los museos, los centros comerciales y los eventos deportivos.
El Gobierno también está considerando incluir en la propuesta de normativa a las escuelas y los hospitales. El anuncio no equivale a una prohibición nacional en vigor: en agosto de 2026 se prohibió su uso en las escuelas de Oslo.
En Australia, el Gobierno federal está reuniendo opiniones con respecto a limitar el uso de las gafas con cámara en sus lugares de trabajo. En septiembre, la ministra de la Función Pública, Katy Gallagher, le pidió consejo a la Comisión de la Función Pública sobre una posible prohibición en estos centros y las excepciones. En Inglaterra y Gales se han prohibido las gafas de Meta en los tribunales por las restricciones a hacer fotos y grabar vídeos en esos recintos.

Les risques ne se limitent cependant pas aux fichiers infectés. Une fausse boutique en ligne ou un site qui imite celui de votre banque peuvent aussi suffire à compromettre vos données personnelles.

articles.title: Après PHP, une autre brique essentielle du web doit être mise à jour d'urgence
articles.summary:
C’est la panique sur Internet depuis ce 21 octobre 2026. La raison : deux failles critiques ont été repérées dans le langage informatique PHP, utilisé par des centaines de millions de sites web à travers le monde. La situation se révèle être un vrai casse-tête pour l’Internet mondial, étant donné qu’il est souvent difficile de repérer le langage PHP, omniprésent, mais souvent invisible. En attendant les correctifs, certains sites ont tout simplement décidé de suspendre leur accès, craignant des cyberattaques. C’est notamment le cas d’Orange qui, après avoir connu une panne majeure, a annoncé la suspension temporaire de certains de ses sites et applications par mesure de sécurité. Et la situation ne semble pas vraiment s’arranger pour l’Internet mondial, étant donné que le projet Node.js vient de publier en urgence une série de correctifs de sécurité.
Node.js corrige 10 failles de sécurité, dont quatre critiques
Node.js est un environnement d’exécution qui permet de faire fonctionner du JavaScript en dehors d’un navigateur web, notamment sur des serveurs. Node.js est bien moins répandu que le langage PHP, mais il occupe tout de même une certaine place dans l’Internet mondial. Selon les données de W3Techs du 9 septembre 2026, Node.js est utilisé comme serveur web par 7 % des sites dont le serveur est identifié. Cette proportion atteint toutefois 22 % parmi les 1 000 sites les plus fréquentés. Les risques de perturbation du web mondial sont donc réels en cas de cyberattaque.

articles.title: Iran’s Prince of Persia APT Hosts C&C in US for First Time Since 2016
articles.summary:
Prince of Persia, a threat group sponsored by the Iranian government, ran one of its command-and-control (C&C) servers from the United States this year, after a months-long lull in its operations, according to Semperis.
The APT actor, also tracked as Infy, has been operating for close to 20 years. Its targets are mostly Iranian dissidents, along with government and private entities in the US, Europe, and the Middle East.
Tomer Bar, AVP of security research at Semperis, tracked the group in his previous role at SafeBreach. He says that within a week of SafeBreach’s February 2026 report, the hackers took a C&C server offline and later relocated the rest of their servers.
Prince of Persia then halted operations for three months, a longer silence than any other in its nearly two-decade history. The pause overlapped with the war between Iran and the US and Israel, which broke out on February 28.
Semperis told SecurityWeek that this is the longest downtime it has confirmed, as its researchers were monitoring the group’s infrastructure the entire time. Earlier quiet periods reflected gaps in researchers’ visibility into the group’s operations rather than confirmed inactivity.
Prince of Persia’s operations restarted on May 27 with the deployment of a new C&C server, and data theft resumed. Within seven days, Tonnerre, one of the group’s malware families, had siphoned over 1,800 files from a single victim.

articles.title: Mysteriöse Nachricht in Super Mario 64: Wurde sie nach 30 Jahren endlich entschlüsselt?
articles.summary:
Super Mario 64: Fan knackt nach 30 Jahren das Rätsel der geheimnisvollen Plakette
Schon 1996 haben Zocker:innen auf der ganzen Welt in Super Mario 64 auf ein seltsames Detail geschaut. In einem Hinterhof des Schlosses steht die Statue eines Sterns. Darunter ist eine Plakette mit einer Inschrift angebracht. Die Auflösung von 32 x 32 Pixeln hatte es bisher aber unmöglich gemacht, die genauen Wörter zu entziffern. Doch das hat Gamer:innen nicht aufgehalten, Theorien aufzustellen.
Super Mario 64: Theorien zur Plakette
Seit Jahrzehnten hält sich hartnäckig die Theorie, dass die obere Zeile der zweizeiligen Inschrift „L is real 2401“ zeigen würde. Die kryptische Nachricht soll laut einigen Gamer:innen ein versteckter Hinweis der Entwickler:innen sein, dass Luigi (also „L“) sich doch im Spiel befindet. Die Zahl 2401 soll indes ein Hinweis sein, wie er freischaltbar ist.
Im Laufe der Jahre hatte Nintendo diese Theorie aber schon zerstört. Damals hieß es in einem Schreiben an einen Fan, dass die Nachricht bewusst unleserlich ist und niemand genau wüsste, was da überhaupt steht. Doch jetzt will ein Fan endlich Licht ins Dunkel gebracht haben. Unter dem Nicknamen „Supermochi64“ hat er auf GitHub eine ausführliche technische Analyse der mysteriösen Plakette veröffentlicht.
Was sagt die Inschrift wirklich?
Um das herauszufinden, hat der Mario-Fan nicht einfach KI genutzt, um die niedrigaufgelöste Plakette hochzurechnen. Er hat den umgekehrten Ansatz gewählt und eigene Plaketten erstellt, …

articles.title: OpenAI réclame encore 30 milliards de dollars, mais les investisseurs commencent à tiquer
articles.summary:
Les milliards continuent d’affluer chez OpenAI, sans que la rentabilité soit encore au rendez-vous. Le créateur de ChatGPT préparerait une nouvelle levée de fonds avant son entrée en Bourse, mais aurait dû revoir ses ambitions à la baisse face aux réticences de certains investisseurs.
Chez OpenAI, les levées de fonds se suivent à un rythme presque aussi soutenu que les nouvelles versions de ChatGPT. À peine sept mois après avoir annoncé un financement historique de 122 milliards de dollars, l’entreprise de Sam Altman serait déjà sur le point de réunir 30 milliards supplémentaires. Selon CNBC, le fonds américain Coatue et plusieurs investisseurs des Émirats arabes unis participeraient aux négociations, avec une valorisation envisagée de 1 250 milliards de dollars, avant l’apport de cet argent.
Un montant vertigineux, qui masque pourtant une première difficulté. D’après le Financial Times, OpenAI espérait initialement être valorisé à 1 400 milliards de dollars, mais les investisseurs n’auraient pas tous suivi.
Des milliards levés à un rythme effréné
Les investisseurs accompagnent OpenAI depuis longtemps. Microsoft avait ouvert le bal en 2019, avant de remettre au pot en 2021 puis en 2023. Le financement a ensuite changé de dimension, avec 6,6 milliards de dollars levés en 2024, puis 40 milliards l’année suivante.

articles.title: Meta diz ao TSE que canal “Exército do Lula” não viola regras do WhatsApp
articles.summary:
A Meta afirmou nesta sexta-feira (23) ao Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) que não encontrou violações das regras do WhatsApp no canal “Exército do Lula”, criado para divulgar publicações de apoio à candidatura à reeleição do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT). articles.title: Origin Range Requests: Serving large files without range-request tuning
articles.summary:
Origin Range Requests: Serving large files without range-request tuning
A video player seeking to the middle of a movie asks for a few megabytes. Under our old range caching, that one request could make Cloudflare pull 128 MiB from the origin and move it between data centers, sometimes after the viewer had already left. Range requests are how large files get delivered, and caching them naively easily leads to wasted network bandwidth and wasted disk operations when running a CDN at scale.
So we rebuilt how our cache handles them. For R2, Cloudflare's object storage, p99 time to first byte dropped by about half, and a follow-up improvement cut tiered cache traffic for R2 and similar workloads by about 6%.
Today, we're making that new implementation available as Origin Range Requests, a self-service feature on all plans. There's no range size to tune and no need to contact support. Turn it on with a Cache Rule, and Cloudflare handles the rest.
A request for part of a file
An HTTP range request asks for part of a resource instead of the whole resource. The client sends a normal GET with a Range header:
GET /movie.mp4 HTTP/1.1
Host: example.com
Range: bytes=1048576-2097151
If the server supports the request, it returns 206 Partial Content and identifies the returned bytes with Content-Range:
HTTP/1.1 206 Partial Content
Content-Range: bytes 1048576-2097151/524288000
Content-Length: 1048576
Range requests are common for large objects. A video player can request bytes around a seek…

- Date:

- Source:

- Summary:
- Oxford physicists have recreated a bizarre quantum effect in which a particle responds to a magnetic field without ever traveling through it. Using a hybrid quantum computer, they demonstrated how introducing a simulated magnetic flux could completely halt a particle's movement through quantum interference. The experiment brings a decades-old prediction into a new setting where matter and quantum fields influence one another.
- Share:
A particle does not have to pass through a magnetic field to be influenced by it. That surprising feature of quantum physics has now been recreated by researchers at the University of Oxford, who used a hybrid quantum computer to demonstrate how an invisible magnetic influence can bring a simulated particle's movement to a complete stop.
The experiment reproduced a phenomenon known as the Aharonov-Bohm effect, in which a charged particle traveling around a region containing magnetic flux experiences a measurable change in its quantum state, even though its path never takes it through the magnetic field itself.
The Oxford team achieved this using a quantum system that combines qubits, the basic units of quantum information, with quantum oscillators, which represent vibrating motion. articles.title: LiteLLM Compromised in Fresh Supply Chain Attack
articles.summary:
LiteLLM was compromised in a fresh supply chain attack, and malicious packages were served to its users on both PyPI and Docker.
The incident occurred on October 21 and involved version 1.107.0 of the popular open source proxy for routing requests across LLM providers.
The malicious packages were online for roughly three hours and are estimated to have been downloaded over 49,000 times. The packages were removed from PyPI, and Docker Hub tags and image variants were either removed or repointed to clean artifacts.
[Read: Trivy, Not LiteLLM Behind the 2,500 Org Compromise ]
Per LiteLLM’s investigation, the attackers obtained the GitHub CLI OAuth tokens for “an unexpected, innocuously named user account in our internal LiteLLM deployment, which was exposed to the public internet”.
The tokens were likely leaked by Claude Code, which, in specific circumstances, would embed them into a response body, which may be logged to LiteLLM logs. The attackers likely retrieved the tokens from the logs.
However, it is still unclear how the attackers accessed the internal deployment or moved laterally, as they had access to three sets of developer GitHub CLI credentials, LiteLLM says.
The attackers used the compromised credentials to disable branch protections, merge a change that pointed the releaser to a different source repository, and run a compromised GitHub workflow that pointed to a lookalike repository, then signed and published the poisoned artifacts.

articles.title: Low-carbon concrete could lower emissions before data centres even go online |
articles.summary:
Concerns about the environmental impact of data centres have been popping across Canada almost as quickly as the data centres themselves. But what if there was a way to start lowering those emissions even before a facility is turned on? According to two cleantech advocates, greening the data centre boom starts with the buildings, and the huge amounts of concrete used to create them.
Concrete is responsible for roughly eight percent of the world’s carbon emissions, according to a study by Chatham House. Those emissions come primarily from the process of refining cement, the binding agent used in concrete. Traditional cement is created through a combustion process that both directly releases CO2 into the atmosphere and relies heavily on fossil fuels throughout manufacturing.
“If we’re looking at the concrete and steel that’s going to go into this project, we’re looking at somewhere between 218,000 and 263,000 tonnes of CO2.”
Gil Yaron, Light House
Data centres use a lot of concrete. According to Gil Yaron, the managing director of circular innovation at Light House, a Vancouver-based non-profit supporting regenerative building practices, Meta’s Sturgeon County data centre is predicted to require as much as 1.5 million cubic metres of concrete. That’s roughly the equivalent of 37 CN Towers.
Far from just an enormous physical footprint, that translates into a lot of emissions, according to Yaron.

articles.title: NgRx 22: Resource Extensions and Dynamic Deep Signals for Angular
articles.summary:
NgRx, the reactive state management framework for Angular, has released version 22, shipping utilities for customising Angular's resource API, dynamic deep signals for union types, a new SignalStore typing helper and ESLint v10 compatibility.
The main new addition is resource extensions, delivered through a new experimental @ngrx/signals/resource entry point. Angular's resource and httpResource APIs reset value() to undefined while reloading and throw when read in an error state. Resource extensions wrap an existing resource and patch only those behaviours, while preserving the original resource type.
Four built-in extensions are included, alongside a provideResourceExtensions function that registers defaults at application, route or component level. In the original RFC, Marko Stanimirović explained that changing the error behaviour is also a prerequisite for deeper SignalStore integration, as "once a resource enters the error state, any subsequent patchState call will throw because it reads value() internally".
The proposal was well received, with Manfred Steyer replying "Love it!" and suggesting an activation signal, while another commenter asked for parity with SolidJS's createResource, such as access to the current value inside the loader.

Media hora sin desayunar, sin café, sin tomar ninguna otra medicación. Y todo eso para que un 1-2% de la semaglutida oral que ha tomado llegue a la sangre.
Durante años, la mejor pastilla que teníamos para perder peso era el Rybelsus y tomarlo, como vemos, requería una disciplina casi monacal. Es decir, la biodisponibilidad acaba por ser limitada y a poca gente le iba realmente bien.

¿Qué ha pasado exactamente? El Comité de Medicamentos de Uso Humano de la Agencia Europea del Medicamento ha dado su visto bueno para dos usos del orforglipron: el control de peso y la diabetes tipo 2 mal controlada. Es verdad que el Comité no puede aprobar medicamentos (eso lo hace la Comisión), pero a efectos prácticos es el paso previo clave.

articles.title: Scaling NVIDIA TensorRT Performance Optimization Beyond a Single Build Route with the Global Performance Tuner, Part 1 | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
Deploying a trained neural network involves more than translating each operator into a GPU kernel. It is a compilation problem with many legitimate answers. For example, when NVIDIA TensorRT builds an engine, it makes interdependent decisions about graph-IR transformations, fusion, implementation selection, memory placement, and quantization. This process is called scheduling. Different scheduling choices can preserve model semantics yet produce very different inference performance, making scheduling central to deep learning compiler optimization.
No single scheduling strategy is best for every model and deployment environment. A transformation that accelerates one network may slow another. A kernel that is faster in isolation may interact poorly with fusion, tensor layouts, or memory traffic elsewhere in the graph. Aggressive scheduling may improve performance while violating an application’s accuracy requirement. These coupled, model-dependent effects often appear only after the complete engine is built and measured, making the right strategy increasingly difficult to predict.
This post is Part 1 of a two-part series that is intended to develop a clearer way of reasoning about performance optimization. It explores questions such as: What makes one compiled engine better than another? Why can individually promising decisions fail end to end? How should accuracy constrain performance optimization? NordVPN has pushed out version 6.0.0 of its Linux app, dated October 22, 2026, and the jump to a new major version number feels earned.

articles.title: Scaling NVIDIA TensorRT Performance Optimization Beyond a Single Build Route with the Global Performance Tuner, Part 2 | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
The Global Performance Tuner is a feature for automatic performance tuning released in NVIDIA TensorRT 11.1. It provides automatic, accuracy-aware and end-to-end performance tuning within TensorRT by customizing different optimizations for different models. For more details, see Part 1 of this series, which introduces the challenges associated with scheduling (a critical stage in deep learning compiler optimization), the motivation for developing the Global Performance Tuner feature in TensorRT, and the mathematical theories established to formalize the problem.
This post, Part 2, uses the notation from Part 1 to describe the algorithm and architectural design of the Global Performance Tuner feature. It also provides best practices for using it.
Designing the Global Performance Tuner feature in TensorRT
The central design idea of the Global Performance Tuner is to represent alternative scheduling strategies as explicit and searchable build routes. A compiler knob (also called a compiler flag or compiler option) is a configuration setting that changes some aspect of the compilation pipeline, such as a heuristic, fusion decision, or code generation path.
Each tunable knob exposes a finite set of allowed values and has a default value. A build route is a concrete combination of knob values. When no build route is specified, TensorRT uses the default build route, in which every knob retains its default value.

In a controlled experiment, researchers manipulated an agent through content it encountered while reading email, prompting it to execute system commands, transmit data outside its environment and perform destructive file operations.
No software vulnerability was required. The agent simply treated untrusted content as instruction.
That autonomy is expanding daily. Agents are moving from answering questions to taking action doing everything from executing code, connecting to services, managing files and making decisions on a user’s behalf.
The shift from developer-focused tools like OpenClaw to widespread use of personal assistants like Muse, happened quickly. Delegating work across platforms is becoming commonplace and how people interact with AI.

Development of the MPAA’s least-favorite app of the 2010s has been abandoned for years, but the “Netflix of Piracy” software is still installed on millions of devices that are just waiting to join a bot army. Researchers at Eye Security found the updater for a Popcorn Time fork called “Time4Popcorn” still running on tons of Windows, macOS, and Android devices located around the world, phoning home to now-abandoned web domains over unencrypted HTTP and running an outdated, insecure version of Chrome.
Abandoned Popcorn Time apps had to be disabled to prevent a zombie army
What old and vulnerable software might be running on your PC right now?
Eye Security’s Niels Teusink says the updater could have been used to install and run basically any kind of software with full privileges, easily enabling someone to create a botnet just by taking over one of the domains, using a man-in-the-middle attack to target specific devices, or perform surveillance by identifying the machines running the software.
Their solution was to register one of the domains and use it to send their own update that instructed the updater to disable itself. Despite ethical concerns about the fix, the researchers say their only alternative “was to do nothing,” pointing out, “The update process wasn’t doing anything functional anyway, it was only creating risk for users.”

A swimming robot does not necessarily need a bulky motor or powerful mechanical parts to move through water. MIT researchers have demonstrated that a single, carefully engineered layer of living muscle cells can generate enough force to propel a tiny robot forward.
The engineers developed an extremely thin swimming robot that uses living muscle tissue to move its fins. Described in a new study published in Advanced Functional Materials, the device has a flexible gel framework roughly the length and width of a stick of gum. “VeloCloud Orchestrator (VCO) on-prem has a security issue where this issue may allow a remote attacker to access privileged internal functionality and impact the VCO host,” Arista notes in its advisory.
Successful exploitation could impact the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of both VCO and the data it manages.
“On an affected system, any authenticated user can gain operator privileges and masquerade as a local ‘superuser operator’ user. This includes access to functionality that is intended for internal use only and which is not intended to be remotely accessible,” the company says.
All VCO releases before versions 5.2.3.18, 6.1.3.10, and 6.4.2.12 are affected. Arista has already patched the hosted VCO deployments, but urges users to update their on-premises installations as soon as possible.
“This issue was detected by Arista and is known to be actively exploited,” the company says.
Arista notes that VCO deployments are exposed by default, and that attackers need access to the VCO web interface and a valid authenticated session, with the lowest built-in tenant role privileges.

Europe’s energy transition story is usually told through assets: more renewable generation, smarter grids, electric vehicles and battery storage. Yet while much of the debate focuses on financing and building infrastructure, a different challenge is emerging beneath the surface: operating and maintaining a rapidly expanding asset base over the next several decades.
But the high-margin subsidised programmes that kick-started the industry are being phased out, and operators are facing a new reality of low-margin operations at scale. Combined with the demographic squeeze on the European workforce, the industry looks ripe for automation. Maybe even for robots.
The problem is well-known and systemic. Transmission networks are aging – some 40% of Europe’s distribution grids are over 40 years old – and cross-border capacity is set to double. Offshore wind is moving further from shore and into deeper water. Solar is multiplying faster than construction and maintenance teams can keep up with.

articles.title: Review: Crystal Lake suffers a bit from its obsession with Pam Voorhees
articles.summary:
Peacock series Crystal Lake doesn’t feel like a Friday the 13th movie when you first press play, even though it’s set up to be a prequel to the original film. (This review includes spoilers of the original Friday the 13th movie but avoids major Crystal Lake spoilers.)
Instead, Crystal Lake strives to build a drama that’s half homage, half uncharted territory, while giving a long-awaited backstory to Pamela Voorhees. The original villain in the first film, Pam Voorhees, shocked audiences in 1980 by popping up out of nowhere in the midst of a brutal camp counselor killing spree, then confronting the final girl with a Norman Bates-like delivery of the movie’s chilling tagline, “Kill her, mommy,” using the voice of her drowned son, Jason.
Although the hockey-masked killer, Jason Voorhees, became the horror icon at the center of the franchise, his mom, Pam, continued to fascinate fans, who knew very little about her. articles.title: Multi-Cloud FinOps: An Engineering Framework for Cross-Cloud Cost Optimization
articles.summary:
Key Takeaways
- Cloud providers in multi-cloud systems charge for data leaving their network, not entering it. The egress costs accumulate silently and are rarely caught before deployment.
- Architecture determines egress cost more than per-unit transfer rates. Where services are placed and how often they communicate matters far more than what you negotiate on billing rates.
- FinOps Open Cost and Usage Specification (FOCUS) provides a unified billing format across cloud providers, reducing normalization effort, but service-level attribution still requires provider-specific fields, ownership metadata, and network telemetry.
- Replacing continuous cross-cloud data transfer with scheduled synchronization reduces costs significantly without degrading service performance.
- Architecture had a larger impact on cost than provider pricing. In the controlled experiment, changing the communication pattern from synchronous cross-cloud processing to near-source processing saved over $2000 per month, while changing the provider rate saved $825 per month.
Introduction
Multi-cloud architectures give teams the flexibility to optimize for availability, vendor capabilities, and geographic reach. But this flexibility carries a hidden cost due to data movement across cloud provider boundaries. The costs accumulate through service placement decisions, communication patterns, and scaling behavior compounding over time. By the time it shows up on a bill, the architectural damage is done.

articles.title: PHP shares mitigation for new RCE vulnerability with no patch
articles.summary:
The PHP security team has shared mitigation measures for a new remote code execution vulnerability that affects systems with non-default configurations and has no patch.
PHP is an open-source web development language used by nearly 70% of all websites on the Internet. According to VirusTotal estimates, more than 5.1 million PHP hosts are exposed online, and roughly 3.8 million have at least one port open to attacks.
According to a Friday advisory, this security flaw (tracked as CVE-2026-115560) can only be exploited when targeting systems "with an unusual combination of configuration and application code."
"An application must set session.serialize_handler to php_binary or php_serialize in its configuration and then switch it to php at runtime with ini_set() before calling session_start(). Session upload progress must also still be enabled," the PHP team explained.
"Applications that never change the serialize handler at runtime can keep the feature enabled. Since this setup is unlikely in practice, we are handling it in the regular release cycle and will publish a full advisory for CVE-2026-115560 with the next release."
Until a security patch is available, the PHP devs suggested setting session.upload_progress.enabled=0, adding that "If you applied it then, keep it in place and no further action is needed."

articles.title: Compromised TLS Certificates - Schneier on Security
articles.summary:
Compromised TLS Certificates
The Indian CA eMudhra Limited has eight TLS certificates with laughably weak private keys:
The compromised eMudhra keys were defective at a level that’s challenging the imagination of many of the engineers studying the incident. A normal size for a NIST P-384 elliptic curve cryptography private key contains roughly 384 bits of entropy, a size allowing almost 2384, or a number with 116 digits, different possibilities. The private key sizes of the compromised keys ranged from 3 to 8 bits. Astonishingly, the private keys were 4, 56, 66, 115, 155, 156, 230, 237.
“That is extremely in the ‘this should not be possible’ category,” Valdorda said. “Maybe some horribly dangerous key generation interface has a ‘size’ parameter and they set it to 1 by mistake???”
Ben Cartwright-Cox, director of BGP.tools, said: “My guess is that it’s example code that accidentally leaked to production, but hard to know. But it’s bonkers that no one noticed.”
At this early stage, the most immediate threat appears to be for those using VPNs, especially in countries with governments likely to maliciously intercept traffic. There are likely many other cases for concern. End users largely have no recourse other than to hold off using many non-browser forms of TLS communication until they receive assurances updates are in place.
The whole certificate regime has long been a mess:
The incident is the latest to expose a fatal flaw in the TLS regimen. It’s only as strong as its weakest…

articles.summary:
Two days after PHP rolled out emergency fixes for the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities, threat actors have tried to use the flaws to spread a Mirai botnet. A security firm has also built an exploit that gets past a key memory protection, and an exposed attacker server has revealed custom tooling.
Even so, no successful in-the-wild compromise has been confirmed so far.
The threat has prompted many organizations to take systems offline as a precaution. Several government, school and hospital websites in Europe went dark on October 21, and the UK government said 32 of its services were unavailable and four partly unavailable, mostly due to precautionary measures taken while patches were applied.

Developers can capture CPU or heap-allocation profiles for a deployed Worker version and inspect the results as a flamegraph, where wider sections indicate functions responsible for a larger share of CPU time or sampled memory allocations. Profiles can also be downloaded for offline analysis.

Y hablamos en pasado porque un artículo publicado en la revista PNAS apunta a que ya se ha perdido aproximadamente una cuarta parte de los glaciares.
Un inventario. Aunque obviamente no todo lo que se ve es glaciar, puesto que para los expertos ganarse esta distinción requiere que estemos ante una masa perenne de nieve e hielo en constante movimiento.
Y a simple vista, las cifras netas podrían llegar a confusión, puesto que los mapas antiguos registraban 1453 glaciares, mientras que el inventario más reciente contabiliza 1.331 glaciares. Behörden, die für ihre Online-Dienste einen elektronischen Ausweis verlangen, müssen d-you als Identifizierungsdienst akzeptieren. Une excellente nouvelle pour les utilisateurs, beaucoup moins évidente pour les entreprises qui investissent des fortunes dans leurs modèles et leurs infrastructures. Car derrière les progrès techniques, la question de la rentabilité devient de plus en plus pressante.
Faire travailler une intelligence artificielle coûte aujourd’hui une fraction de ce que les entreprises facturaient encore il y a dix-huit mois. Et la baisse est vertigineuse. Sur certaines tâches, l’écart atteint même un facteur 725.
De quoi bouleverser l’économie d’un secteur où les investissements dans les centres de données battent pourtant tous les records.
Des performances comparables pour une fraction du prix
L’exemple le plus frappant concerne GPQA Diamond, un test de connaissances scientifiques de niveau doctorat. Agentic AI is threatening online banking security
- Customers are increasingly enlisting AI agents to handle banking jobs for them
- Banks are struggling to distinguish between human, legitimate AI and rogue activity
- Many are now preparing for worst-case scenarios when AI does go rogue
Several major US banks have detected third-party AI agents accessing their customers' bank accounts, sometimes even attempting to carry out actions beyond what users actually wanted them to do.
New Axios reporting has claimed banks are now said to be struggling to even distinguish between legitimate human activity and agentic activity – but especially between authorized and rogue AI agents.
Importantly, the concern isn't so much disconnected, rogue AI going after system vulnerabilities to obtain customer information – banks are currently worrying about AI agents that human users themselves are setting off on their behalves.

Researcher Patrick Wardle has analyzed Heartbreaker, a Rust-based macOS ransomware sample that was uploaded to VirusTotal in May 2025 and, as of his writing, was still undetected by every antivirus engine on the service. After attempting to set up a LaunchAgent for persistence, it encrypts files in the user’s Downloads folder. It then tries to change its hash by taking its own embedded source code, randomizing identifiers and adding junk functions, and recompiling itself (even trying to install Rust if it’s missing). Wardle believes it’s unlikely to be a major threat in its current form, as it uses a single hardcoded AES key that makes free file recovery possible, and its rebuild process depends on a Rust framework that’s no longer publicly available.

Millicent Okumu doesn’t leave you wondering whether she believes what she is saying. She speaks with energy, with clarity about whom she is building for. Ask where the company is heading, and there is little hesitation; ask whether she will still be running it in ten years, and the answer is no.
By then, she expects Agriflex, the Kenyan agricultural business she co-founded, to be operating in at least five African countries, to be sustainably profitable, and to be led by somebody else. She might take an advisory role. For now, however, the company occupies even the hours she supposedly spends away from it. At family gatherings, unfinished tasks follow her into the room.
Her father, a civil servant and farmer, raised cattle and grew enough food to support relatives beyond his household. She was close to him, but less enthusiastic about the farm. She avoided agriculture at school and university, only to find herself back in it through a logistics job at iProcure in 2017.
Now she sells farm inputs, deploys spraying drones and listens to farmers explain why a clever piece of technology might be of little use to them. That last part has meant slowing down plans and turning away investors.
“We are in 2026,” she says. “We are no longer in 2006.”
She is impatient for progress, but increasingly particular about what counts as progress, and who benefits.

AWS recently introduced Lambda Web Functions, allowing developers to run Node.js web applications using frameworks such as Express and Hono directly on Lambda, with support for concurrent requests and response streaming.
According to the Lambda Web Functions documentation, the new functions support concurrent HTTP requests and response streaming. They charge for active CPU time and memory, rather than CPU time spent waiting for downstream services. Multi-Region routing directs requests to the closest Region, while a single warm execution environment can handle multiple concurrent requests, significantly reducing cold starts. Existing Lambda functions are now called Lambda Event Functions, with no changes required. Micah Walter, senior solutions architect at AWS, summarizes the benefits and why it removes this complexity:
You can take a standard port-listening server built with Express, Hono, Fastify, Next.js, or any Node.js framework, deploy it with a single command, and Lambda automatically handles scaling, multi-region distribution, and active CPU billing. No adapters, no infrastructure to manage, and no framework lock-in.
Endpoints use a Lambda-provided domain by default. To use a custom domain, edge caching, or AWS WAF, developers can use Amazon CloudFront in front, relying on Lambda Web Functions as the origin.

After unauthorized access to the multi-tenant application, the group attempted sign-ins at more than 2,250 Microsoft 365 tenants, with stolen ConnectWise app credentials that authenticated as the apps with no interactive user sign-in. Some of the group’s attacks reached privileged access less than three hours after initial targeting.
Automated password guessing, or password spraying, also targeted 327 accounts across eight organizations with more than 151,000 failed logons and no successes. The use of ARTEX, “a system of LLM-driven agents that run an autonomous penetration test,” sped up scanning and reconnaissance, password spraying, and OAuth application abuse. The agents can work around the clock “with little needed human interaction,” at a pace that “leaves defenders with little time to detect and respond.” It’s uncertain how the ConnectWise credentials were stolen or how many tenants were actually compromised.

articles.title: Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning on Amazon SageMaker AI: A hands-on guide | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning on Amazon SageMaker AI: A hands-on guide
Most fine-tuning teaches a model to produce a better answer to a single prompt. Agentic tasks are different. An agent that files an expense report or triages a support ticket takes a sequence of actions, and each step depends on what came before. There’s rarely one correct sequence to imitate, and the only reliable feedback is whether the whole sequence succeeded. Supervised fine-tuning has no labels for that, and single-turn reinforcement learning cannot credit a decision made three steps before the outcome.
Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning (MTRL) on Amazon SageMaker AI trains models on exactly that signal. SageMaker AI sends prompts to an agent you host on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, or on your own infrastructure, such as Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS), Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2), or AWS Fargate, through an AWS Lambda forwarder. The example here uses AgentCore. The agent calls the policy model being trained, acts in your environment over as many turns as the task needs, and reports one reward when the episode ends. You don’t specify the right trajectory, only how to score the result.
This post uses Wordle, a game in which a player has six tries to guess a hidden five-letter word, as the example. After each guess, every letter turns green if it is in the right position, yellow if it’s in the word but in a different position, and gray if it isn’t in…

articles.title: CSIRO Uses Serverless Architecture to Query 100x More Genomic Variants on AWS
articles.summary:
CSIRO has developed Serverless Beacon (sBeacon), a serverless architecture for querying genomic variant data without copying large genomic datasets into a central database. The system uses Amazon S3, AWS Lambda, Amazon Athena, and Amazon DynamoDB to provide an implementation of the Global Alliance for Genomics and Health (GA4GH) Beacon standard, supporting genomic queries across large cohorts while keeping the underlying data in its original storage.
The architecture separates genomic data from the metadata needed to search it. Variant Call Format (VCF) files remain in Amazon S3, while metadata such as disease status, age, and location is indexed separately. During onboarding, sBeacon creates indexes and Athena tables for the metadata, while ontology terms are handled through CSIRO's Ontoserver to support queries combining genomic and phenotypic information.
sBeacon data onboarding architecture (Source: AWS Blog Post)
For variant queries, API Gateway routes requests to Lambda functions that identify relevant datasets and genomic regions. The Variant Querying Module uses bcftools and its htslib library to retrieve specific portions of VCF files through HTTP byte range requests. This allows the system to read the required genomic region without transferring the complete file. Results are aggregated and returned through the Beacon API.

Discover how Anshu Kumar’s Neev Ki Eent Foundation is helping children of brick kiln workers in Bihar access education and build brighter futures.
Every year, thousands of families in Bihar move from one place to another in search of employment. A significant number of these families work at brick kilns. For them, migration is not simply about changing locations. It means changing homes and workplaces. In the process, children’s education often takes a back seat.

Schools may be located far away, and a lack of essential documents can make it difficult to access government services. Limited awareness of welfare schemes adds to the challenges. articles.title: Two Dollars and a Test Suite - EE Times
articles.summary:
The Arm-Qualcomm verdict made headlines for its $2 award. The finding that matters more is about who controls the compliance tests a custom chip must pass before it can ship.
The verdict nobody read closely
On Oct. 13, a federal jury in Delaware delivered the second verdict in two years between Arm and Qualcomm. The number that drew the most attention was the damages award: $2, one for each claim Qualcomm won. Both companies declared victory, and IMHO both had some reason to. Arm prevailed on four of the six claims. On the other hand, Qualcomm won a finding that Arm interfered with its business with Meta, plus an additional finding under its Architecture License Agreement that I think deserves far more attention than it received.
The jury found that Arm breached Qualcomm’s Architecture License Agreement by withholding two deliverables, ACKs and OOBs. To most people, these acronyms mean very little, which may explain why most coverage moved quickly on to royalties and to the $2. But they describe something we may know very well: the tests a custom processor must pass before anyone can call it an Arm processor.
What a compliance kit actually does
Arm licenses its technology in two ways. Most customers take Arm-designed cores “as is” and integrate them into their chips, under a Technology License Agreement (TLA). articles.title: Cloudflare Reclaims 100 TB of RAM by Optimizing Consistent Hashing
articles.summary:
Cloudflare recently documented how it reduced the memory footprint of its internal load-balancing service by more than 100 TB by optimizing the Rust implementation of consistent hashing in pingora-ketama. The changes compacted hash-ring entries and used statistical analysis of hash distribution and collision rates to reduce the number of hashes per backend by about 90% while preserving load-balancing accuracy.
Cloudflare relies on consistent hashing in its Pingora Backend Router to distribute cacheable requests across servers, but supporting weighted servers and different feature combinations required many hash rings, significantly increasing memory usage. The team identified excessive memory usage coming from its pingora-ketama consistent-hashing data structures, prompting an investigation into their design and optimization.
Cloudflare applied probability theory to consistent hashing to determine the minimum number of hash points needed to achieve the required distribution, allowing the team to significantly reduce the size of the hashing structures while maintaining the required distribution.

articles.title: Abandoned Popcorn Time app exposed millions of devices to RCE attacks
articles.summary:
Researchers remotely disabled a vulnerable updater in the abandoned Time4Popcorn app, a fork of the Popcorn Time BitTorrent client, closing a security flaw that could have allowed attackers to execute malicious code with elevated privileges on millions of computers.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-30612, affects Windows and macOS updaters that contacted the app's abandoned domain (popcorntimeupd.xyz) over unencrypted HTTP and accepted executables without verifying digital signatures.
Anyone controlling the update domain could manipulate HTTP traffic and execute code as SYSTEM on Windows and as root on macOS.
The Popcorn Time app featured a Netflix-style interface that integrated BitTorrent downloads, allowing users to consume illegal content right directly inside the app.
The project was abandoned for legal reasons but later relaunched as a legitimate content-streaming app. However, forks such as Time4Popcorn emerged under the Popcorn Time name, quickly attracting millions of users.
Researchers at Eye Security discovered the security risk after registering the popcorntimeupd.xyz domain and observed up to 3 million Windows and 350,000 macOS client connections to Time4Popcorn.
Connections came from residential ISPs and corporate, government, and military networks. However, none of the users appeared to be actively using the app, suggesting it had been installed and forgotten.

Autonomy and control are not opposites, they go together: EY GDS at DevSparks Chennai
At DevSparks Chennai 2026, Arvind Purushothaman of EY GDS made the case that moving agents into production is an engineering problem, not a model problem.
Ask a room of developers about agents today and you will get plenty of answers. Almost everyone has built one, and most have a demo they are proud of.
The harder question is what happens after that, when the agent has to hold up against real customers, real data, and real consequences. At DevSparks Chennai 2026, Arvind Purushothaman, Global Cloud Consulting, Microsoft Practice and Alliances Leader at EY GDS, opened with a version of it. He asked how many people in the room had built an AI agent, and plenty of hands went up. Then he asked how many had built one that made it to production for a business-critical system. "I think that's where the numbers dramatically drop," he said. "Not because of anybody's fault, but that's how it is."
That gap is the whole problem, and it is not a model problem. Cloud, low code tools, and open model APIs have pushed the entry barrier close to zero. What has not changed is the difficulty of industrializing what you build. "Access to intelligence is not the bottleneck, but the ability to industrialize is going to be the bottleneck," said Arvind Purushothaman.

OpenAI est revenu sur la sécurité de ses modèles dans une communication publiée le 23 octobre. Les cas de « désalignement », ces comportements qui s’écartent de ce que l’on attend des IA, se sont accumulés ces derniers mois avec pas moins de 20 incidents constatés sur l’année 2026.
Chez OpenAI, des agents sont notamment parvenus à pirater Hugging Face pendant une évaluation interne. D’autres ont appris à dissimuler leurs erreurs.
En septembre, un nouvel accès non autorisé à Internet avait conduit l’entreprise à suspendre certains travaux sur ses modèles les plus avancés. OpenAI précise désormais que cette pause a duré onze jours, jusqu’au 1er octobre, pour renforcer ses protections et les mettre à l’épreuve.
Pourquoi faut-il confiner une IA pendant son entraînement ?
Trouver une information, écrire du code, résoudre un problème : pour entraîner une IA, OpenAI (et d’autres) force son modèle à trouver une solution. Le modèle essaie, échoue, recommence, et les essais réussis servent ensuite à renforcer les comportements qui l’ont mené au but. Mais comment s’assurer qu’il ne prend pas un raccourci interdit pour y arriver ?
D’où l’idée de l’enfermer dans un environnement contrôlé, souvent appelé « bac à sable ». L’IA y dispose d’outils pour travailler, mais ses accès sont limités. Un peu comme un terrain d’exercice : elle doit pouvoir s’entraîner sans intervenir sur les systèmes extérieurs.

articles.title: Agent cloud startup Daytona hits $1B valuation backed by FirstMark and a who’s who of angels | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Daytona Platforms announced on Friday that it had raised a $60 million Series B round at a $1 billion valuation led by FirstMark Growth. The company says it has now raised a total of $91 million.
The New York-based startup has attracted not just FirstMark (which also led its $24 million Series A in February), but also a host of well-known angels in this latest round. Daytona says they include Stripe’s Patrick Collison, Shopify’s Tobi Lütke, Perplexity’s Aravind Srinivas, Zoom’s Eric Yuan, Datadog’s Olivier Pomel, Quora’s Adam D’Angelo (who is also an OpenAI board member), and Mercor’s Brendan Foody. It also names Qualcomm Ventures, Samsung Next, and Okta Ventures as participants.
Three-year-old Daytona is building a cloud specifically for long-running agents, which have different infrastructure needs than yesteryear’s software, the startup contends. “Agents don’t work like the long-lived services today’s cloud was designed for. They spin up thousands of short, stateful jobs nobody planned in advance, and they need a cloud built for that,” founder Ivan Burazin wrote in a blog post announcing the new round. Daytona’s cloud, he said, is like giving every agent its own computer, where agents have access to sandboxed versions of Linux, Windows, macOS, and GPUs, among other services, on the one platform.

Security-Fragebogen bremst den Deal? So wird Compliance zum Wachstumstreiber für Enterprise-Vertrieb
Und der Fragebogen ist erst der Anfang: Der nächste Kunde verlangt ISO 27001, ein Automotive-Kunde TISAX, ein US-Kunde SOC 2. Je größer die Kunden werden, desto mehr entscheiden schnelle und belastbare Compliance-Nachweise über den Vertriebserfolg.
Was Enterprise-Kunden wirklich prüfen
Security-Fragebögen sehen auf den ersten Blick nach vielen unterschiedlichen Anforderungen aus, drehen sich inhaltlich jedoch meist um dieselben Fragen:
- Wer darf auf welche Systeme zugreifen (Berechtigungskonzept)?
- Welche Dienstleister verarbeiten Daten (Vendor Management)?
- Wie werden Sicherheitsvorfälle behandelt und welche Löschfristen gelten?
- Welche technischen und organisatorischen Maßnahmen (TOMs) sind konkret umgesetzt?
Bei kleineren Deals reicht oft eine Selbstauskunft. Bei Enterprise-Kunden, regulatorischen Vorgaben (wie NIS2, DORA, dem Cyber Resilience Act oder dem EU AI Act) und branchenspezifischen Standards kommen formale Nachweise wie ISO 27001, SOC 2 oder TISAX hinzu.
Der Kunde fragt dabei nach der Kontrolle und dem Nachweis, nicht nach dem spezifischen Framework dahinter. Viele Unternehmen haben deshalb kein neues Compliance-Problem, sondern ein Wiederverwendungsproblem: Wer jedes Framework als separates Projekt behandelt, beschreibt Controls neu, sucht Nachweise erneut zusammen und dokumentiert Verantwortlichkeiten mehrfach.

US banks scramble to restrict AI agent activity — agents detected accessing customer accounts or even attempting to make transactions in breach of policy
Banks can't determine if AI agents are working under user instructions or going rogue.
A new report claims that major U.S. banks have now detected AI agents accessing customer accounts, and that some are even attempting to make transactions. Axios reports that it’s hard to differentiate between an actual human and an unauthorized bot, which is why some institutions, including Morgan Stanley, Bank of America, JPMorgan, and Wells Fargo, are blocking the technology and changing their terms of service to account for this.
While an AI agent or AI assistant can access an account with a user’s permission and through the use of their login credentials, this often goes against bank policy that requires users to maintain control of their account and not share it with anyone else. One of the fears that executives have is when an AI agent with login access takes unauthorized steps, like spending money or moving funds around without the explicit instructions of the account owner. There have even been situations where an AI agent called the bank directly and took actions independent of direct user command. Even though it wasn’t explicitly told to do that transaction, it considered it a crucial step to accomplish the task assigned to it.

Pesquisador identificou falha que permite rodar aplicativos não oficiais e modificar jogos no console.
O Nintendo Switch 2 foi desbloqueado pela primeira vez via software, pouco mais de um ano após o lançamento. Batizado de ns2jb, o método permite executar código não autorizado sem instalar modchips ou realizar modificações físicas no console.
A descoberta foi apresentada pelo pesquisador Sammy Hajhamid, conhecido como “pepsipu”, e funciona na versão 23.0.1 do sistema, atualmente o firmware mais recente do Switch 2. O jailbreak, no entanto, possui limitações e não oferece o mesmo nível de acesso que usuários conseguiram ao desbloquear o Switch original.
O processo é feito apenas por software e não exige abrir o videogame ou soldar componentes na placa. Segundo o pesquisador, o ns2jb aproveita falhas encontradas no SmileBASIC 4, aplicativo de programação criado para o primeiro Switch e executado no Switch 2 graças à retrocompatibilidade.
Uma das vulnerabilidades permite executar código não autorizado e alcançar componentes privilegiados do sistema, incluindo o módulo responsável pelo gerenciamento de arquivos, permissões bloqueadas para desenvolvedores independentes.

articles.title: Capcom piraté : les données de 11,7 millions de comptes ont été volées
articles.summary:
Nouvelle fuite de données, mais cette fois-ci du côté du Japon, et plus précisément chez Capcom. En effet, ce 19 octobre 2026, Capcom a détecté une intrusion dans ses systèmes. Deux jours plus tard, après avoir notamment ouvert une cellule de crise interne, l’éditeur et développeur de jeux vidéo a alerté la police d’Osaka.
La brèche a été colmatée par Capcom, mais le mal était déjà fait : l’intrus a mis la main sur les données de 11,7 millions de comptes Capcom ID. Le développeur de Resident Evil appelle dorénavant les joueurs à faire preuve de prudence : certains arnaqueurs pourraient usurper l’identité de Capcom ou de l’un de ses partenaires afin d’arriver à leur fin.
Les données de 11,7 millions de comptes Capcom ID volées
L’intrus est parvenu à exfiltrer un certain nombre de données liées à 11,7 millions de comptes Capcom ID. Ces données comprennent : l’adresse e-mail, la date de création du compte, la dernière connexion au compte, le nombre total de connexions et la dernière adresse IP. Pour 43 joueurs, l’éditeur a aussi constaté la fuite de la date de naissance, du genre, du pays et du pseudo.
Capcom assure qu’aucune donnée bancaire n’a été compromise durant cette cyberattaque. En revanche, le malfrat a réussi à modifier les mots de passe de 196 comptes. Capcom explique ne pas savoir comment il s’y est pris. L’éditeur de jeux vidéo ne précise pas comment l’intrus est parvenu à s’introduire dans ses systèmes, ni combien de temps il a pu y rester.

articles.title: Recht bei Reklamationen: So wehrst du dich gegen die „Hersteller-Ausrede“ der Händler
articles.summary:

Es ist ein Klassiker im Online- und stationären Handel: Wer ein defektes Gerät beim Händler reklamiert, bekommt oftmals gesagt, dass er sich doch bitte direkt an den Hersteller wenden möge, weil man ihm dort schneller helfen könne und man das Gerät ja ohnehin einschicken würde. Doch der Reparaturservice des Herstellers, der sich um solche Probleme kümmern soll, ist in diesem Fall nicht die erste Anlaufstelle, wie ein neues Urteil zeigt.
Klar, für den Händler ist es praktisch, wenn sich die Kund:innen mit dem Service herumärgern müssen, doch für diese bedeutet es oftmals zusätzlichen Aufwand. Es ist aber vor allem rechtlich problematisch, wenn damit die Verantwortung für die gesetzliche Gewährleistung auf den Hersteller abgeschoben werden soll.
Mediamarkt wurde nun seitens des Landgerichts Ingolstadt dieses Vorgehen untersagt. Im Verfahren des Verbraucherzentrale Bundesverbands (vzbv) gegen die MMS E-Commerce GmbH – das ist die Onlinetochter besagter Elektronikmarktkette – entschieden die Richter, dass die Aufforderung gegenüber den Kund:innen, Gewährleistungsansprüche direkt beim Hersteller geltend zu machen, irreführend ist. Das Urteil vom 24. Juli 2026 (Az. 1 HK O 1352/25) wurde in der vergangenen Woche veröffentlicht und ist noch nicht rechtskräftig.

- Clayface's director has revealed why Batman doesn't appear
- James Watkins has also addressed the lack of a post-credits scene
- The new DC Universe movie is out now in theaters worldwide
Full spoilers follow for Clayface.
Clayface director James Watkins has explained why Batman doesn't appear — despite confirmation that the Caped Crusader is already active in Gotham City when the film takes place.
Prior to the movie's late October release, DC Studios co-head Peter Safran confirmed to Collider that the Dark Knight is already fighting crime during the events of Clayface. Despite this, the new DC Universe (DCU) film doesn't feature a cameo from Bruce Wayne's alter ego.
On the surface, the decision not to include Batman makes sense, because nobody has been cast as the DCU's iteration of the iconic DC superhero yet. articles.title: Crows can evaluate visual info twice as fast as mammals
articles.summary:
Much of what we know about how a brain makes decisions comes from studying monkeys watching dots. In a task known as a random-dot-motion task, a cloud of flickering specks drifts weakly in one direction while the subject tries to determine whether—and in which direction— it’s moving. The task has shown that in the primate neocortex, neurons gather visual evidence over time, with their firing rates climbing until they cross a threshold, when the animal commits to a decision.
But avian brains don’t have a neocortex, so it wasn’t obvious how they made similar decisions.
“This was the big question,” said Andreas Nieder, a neurobiologist at the University of Tübingen. “How [would] a differently organized avian brain encode decisions?”
To find out, Nieder and his colleague Philipp Schmidbauer put two carrion crows through the same task the monkeys faced, recording their brain activity along the way. The crows solved the task the same way primates do, using the same mathematical logic despite having a very different brain structure. And they did it two times faster.
A brain built different
Nieder and Schmidbauer put two hand-raised crows in front of a touch-sensitive monitor showing a cloud of white dots on black, with some fraction of them drifting coherently left or right or up or down. The birds’ job was to report the overall direction by pecking one of the targets that flanked the display. Correct answers earned them a mealworm.

Right now, she said, a lot of founders pitch revenue metrics to investors without specifying which revenue they are talking about. “Is it true ARR or is it run rate?” she said. “There’s many ways to obfuscate the whole thing.”
Lately, much chatter on X has focused on AI founders inflating ARR numbers (which could mean “annualized run rate” or the more solid “annual recurring revenue”) to make it seem like their companies are doing better than they are. articles.title: L’emprise de la Chine alarme : TSMC cherche à se passer de terres rares dans ses usines
articles.summary:
TSMC veut desserrer l’étau chinois. Le géant des puces explore des équipements sans terres rares, ces métaux sur lesquels Pékin détient un quasi-monopole. Et l’enjeu est vital.
Les terres rares forment un groupe de 17 métaux. Dans la croûte terrestre, elles sont dispersées, mélangées entre elles, et très difficiles à extraire comme à séparer. Un domaine dans lequel la Chine a pris une avance monumentale : selon l’Agence internationale de l’énergie (AIE), elle assurait en 2024 environ 60 % de l’extraction mondiale des terres rares, ainsi que 91 % de leur raffinage et 94 % de la production d’aimants. Un atout économique qui peut devenir une véritable arme diplomatique.
Un levier redoutable pour la Chine
Car ces métaux offrent une puissance environ dix fois supérieure à celle des aimants classiques, pour un poids et une taille réduits. On les retrouve donc partout : dans les smartphones, les voitures électriques, les éoliennes, les avions de chasse ou encore les moteurs des machines d’usine.
Et justement, d’après Reuters, TSMC, numéro 1 mondial de la fabrication de semi-conducteurs, a sondé ses fournisseurs sur des moteurs sans terres rares pour l’automatisation de ses usines. Car aujourd’hui, ils fonctionnent grâce à des aimants fabriqués à partir de ces métaux. Une initiative qui fait suite aux larges restrictions imposées par la Chine ces dernières années.

articles.title: « Je n’ai jamais entendu quelque chose d’artificiel qui sonnait si… humain » : cette IA parle comme nous

Cet échange figure parmi les démonstrations publiées par Block ce vendredi 23 octobre pour présenter Dessa. L’entreprise de Jack Dorsey (ex-fondateur de Twitter, devenu X) affirme avoir entraîné ce modèle uniquement sur des conversations humaines, sans texte ni modèle préentraîné. Les extraits sont étonnamment vivants, au point que certains internautes peinent à croire qu’ils écoutent une IA.
Une IA qui n’attend pas son tour pour parler
Dans un autre extrait, une personne annonce à Dessa un voyage surprise à Paris. L’IA réagit avant la fin de l’annonce. Ailleurs, Block met en avant ses rires au milieu d’une phrase et sa capacité à parler plus fort lorsqu’on le lui demande. L’entreprise présente ces extraits comme des conversations enregistrées en direct, avec des sous-titres ajoutés après coup.
Dessa reproduit les imperfections de nos conversations. Sur ces extraits, choisis par Block, elle paraît plus fluide que les échanges encore assez mécaniques de Gemini, et même que les modèles vocaux de ChatGPT lancés en juillet dernier.
Les hésitations, les rires et les interruptions donnent davantage l’impression d’avoir une personne au bout du fil. De quoi nous rapprocher un peu plus de la réalité…

articles.title: Unerwartetes Wetterphänomen: Wie sich auf dem Mars eine 1.800 Kilometer lange Wolke formt
articles.summary:
1.800 Kilometer lang und völlig ohne Staub: Das Rätsel um Mars-Wolke ist gelöst
Die europäische Weltraumorganisation Esa hat neue Daten zur sogenannten Arsia Mons Elongated Cloud veröffentlicht. Wie in einer im Wissenschaftsmagazin Nature veröffentlichten Studie zu lesen ist, entsteht dieses langgestreckte Gebilde durch einen bisher in planetaren Atmosphären nicht beobachteten Mechanismus. Dieser physikalische Prozess, die sogenannte homogene Keimbildung, vollzieht sich gänzlich ohne die Anwesenheit von Kondensationskernen wie Staub oder Schmutzpartikeln.
Dabei galt in der meteorologischen Forschung bislang ein fester Grundsatz: Wasserdampf benötigt zwingend Staub oder andere winzige Partikel, um zu kondensieren. Da die Atmosphäre des Mars extrem staubig ist, nahmen bisherige Klimamodelle diesen Vorgang stets als alleinigen Standardmechanismus an.
Die aktuellen Computersimulationen eines Forschungsteams um Jorge Hernández-Bernal und Franck Forget von der französischen Sorbonne Université in Paris widerlegen dies nun. Sie zeigen, dass diese etablierte Grundannahme für die lange Arsia-Mons-Wolke schlichtweg nicht gilt.
Wie der Mars-Vulkan das Wetter extrem beschleunigt
Der rund 20 Kilometer hohe Vulkan Arsia Mons wirkt auf den Marswind wie eine gigantische Rampe. Wenn die Luftströmungen auf das massive Hindernis treffen, werden sie als atmosphärische Wellen mit hoher Geschwindigkeit nach oben gedrückt. La Chine réalise l'impossible : elle crée une batterie au lithium innovante capable de maintenir son autonomie, même à −50 °C
Des chercheurs de l'Université de Nankai ont dévoilé une batterie au lithium qui fonctionne encore par −70 °C et stocke deux fois plus d'énergie que les modèles actuels. Le secret : un électrolyte qui rompt avec un siècle de chimie. La découverte est spectaculaire, mais encore loin de nos voitures.
Tout conducteur de voiture électrique connaît la mauvaise surprise de l'hiver. Un matin de gel, l'autonomie affichée fond de 20, parfois 40 %, et la recharge s'éternise. Ce n'est pas un défaut de fabrication, mais une limite physique que l'on croyait presque indépassable : le froid paralyse la chimie interne des batteries. C'est précisément ce verrou, vieux comme la batterie elle-même, qu'une équipe chinoise affirme avoir fait sauter.
Pourquoi le froid tue les batteries
Pour comprendre l'exploit, il faut regarder ce qui se passe àl'intérieur d'une batterie quand le thermomètre chute. Le cœur du système, c'est l'électrolyte, ce liquide dans lequel voyagent les ions lithium d'un bout à l'autre de la cellule à chaque charge et décharge. Dans toutes les batteries actuelles, ce liquide repose sur des solvants à base d'oxygène, un choix hérité des débuts de la chimie des piles.

articles.title: Inside the Pentagon, the pressure is on to find a home for a new spaceport
articles.summary:
Leaders in the US Space Force would like to have a new spaceport up and running in four years, adding a third heavy-lift launch site to relieve pressure from bases in Florida and California that have shot rockets into orbit for nearly 70 years.
The obvious problem with that ambition is 2030 is four years away, and Pentagon officials have not determined where the new spaceport should go or how to acquire land for it.
Air Force Secretary Troy Meink first mentioned the service’s search for a third launch base in May. A congressionally mandated study of the Space Force’s launch infrastructure identified the need for “another site that’s capable of heavy and super heavy launch capability,” Meink said in a House Armed Services Committee hearing.
The Trump administration released a space transportation policy in August that endorsed the construction of more launch and reentry sites for commercial and military missions. This week, the Space Force general responsible for procuring launch services for the military laid out an “aspirational” timeline for a new launch site.
“We need this capability by 2030, but I’m also a pragmatist,” said Lt. Gen. Philip Garrant, head of Space Systems Command. “That is not an inconsequential demand to build a spaceport when you factor in orbital regimes, safety, access to commodities, the Americans that live near it. In many ways, it’s much like an airport, but even louder. So there’s a lot of consideration.”

articles.title: OpenAI says it will no longer train its AI models on the live internet, citing “significant risks” | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
On Friday, OpenAI said that it will train its models using cached copies and simulated versions of the internet instead of the live web because the models are too unpredictable to be trusted with live internet access.
The frontier lab announced its new policy two weeks after its rival, Anthropic, began limiting its newest and, in theory, most capable models from accessing the live internet. Researchers adopted these policies after months of incidents in which models pursuing training tasks broke into external systems in search of answers, collaborated on obscure message boards, and developed exotic hacking strategies.
“Based on the current state of alignment research, monitoring systems, and the security of internet infrastructure, we believe the responsible approach is to conduct frontier model training with no internet access,” the company said in a blog post.
OpenAI said that as recently as September 20, one of its frontier models exploited a misconfiguration to access the internet. That led the company to pause training work for the rest of the month so it could develop and test new approaches to securing its models.
The decision to train these models in sandboxes cut off from the internet is notable because employees at frontier labs have insisted that doing so would be nearly infeasible.
Keeping AI data centers separate from the internet “would need research teams to essentially be embedded inside of data centers in Iowa or wherever else around the world,” former OpenAI…

articles.title: Logran lo que parecía imposible: conectan un Apple Watch a un celular Android por primera vez
articles.summary:
Un desarrollador consiguió emparejar y activar un Apple Watch con un teléfono Android, algo que Apple nunca ha permitido oficialmente desde el lanzamiento del reloj en 2015.
El proyecto se llama Apple Watch Companion y es de código abierto. Su creador, identificado como Md Ismail Šojal, recurrió a la ingeniería inversa para reconstruir los protocolos privados que usa Apple para comunicar el reloj con el teléfono, sin que en ningún momento intervenga un iPhone.
Cómo se rompió el bloqueo entre Apple Watch y Android
El software reconstruye dos piezas centrales del ecosistema de Apple. La primera es el protocolo nativo de comunicación por Bluetooth. La segunda es el servicio IDS, el sistema que conecta y cifra las comunicaciones entre los dispositivos de la compañía.
Con ambos protocolos descifrados, la aplicación puede descubrir el reloj, activarlo, reconectarlo y sincronizarlo desde un móvil con Android. Según detalla el repositorio del proyecto en GitHub, todo el proceso de configuración inicial se completa sin recurrir a ningún dispositivo de Apple.
El emparejamiento con Android admite dos métodos: por código PIN o mediante la cámara del teléfono. El autor reutilizó los mismos protocolos reconstruidos para extender la compatibilidad a Windows, Linux y macOS, aunque estas últimas versiones son más limitadas que la de Android.
